product: Car parts (HS 8708), especially machined parts: brakes, gearboxes, axles, wheels, suspension, steering
local_now: GIAMM (31 Jul 2025): the local supply chain supplies about 55% of a car's value (Thailand about 78%), from about 1,550 suppliers plus 950 SMEs. No separate local share exists for machined parts. Certified electric cars sit at 40-46.5% TKDN (6 firms, Kemenperin TKDN database, 16 Oct 2026). 2025 imports (3,132.2) exceeded exports (2,133.3) (Comtrade, US$M).
local_makers: Astra Otoparts group: Akebono Brake Astra Indonesia, Kayaba Indonesia, Inti Ganda Perdana, Federal Izumi Manufacturing, Federal Nittan Industries, Aisin Indonesia, Astra Komponen Indonesia (plant cities not verified)
PT Dharma Polimetal Tbk (Cikarang Selatan, Kab. Bekasi)
Koperasi Batur Jaya foundries (Ceper, Kab. Klaten)
Tegal metal small firms coached by YDBA (Kab. Tegal)
PT Arkha Industries Indonesia, tier-1 to Astra Komponen Indonesia (city not verified; snippet)
cnc_3d_role: CNC turning and milling of brake discs, drums and calipers, hubs and knuckles, axle shafts, suspension and steering parts, gears and shafts, plus brackets for EV battery and motor mounting. The work is volume tier-2/3 machining under IATF 16949. 3D printing is a support role: jigs, welding fixtures, checking gauges and prototype brackets for the EV models that must reach 60% TKDN in 2027.
potential_share: Judgement, 3-5 years: Indonesian-made share of machined car parts could rise about 5-10 percentage points from GIAMM's ~55% overall local content. That would replace 5-10% of 2025 HS 8708 imports, about US$157-313M (estimate: 0.05 x 3,132.2 and 0.10 x 3,132.2). The most machining-heavy codes (brakes 870830, axles 870850, wheels 870870, suspension 870880, steering 870894) imported US$1,173M in 2025. Gearboxes (870840) stay captive imports of Japanese and Thai groups. Reasoning: the 2027 EV step to 60% TKDN (all certified EV cars are at 40-46.5%), the 1:1 CBU-offset deadline at end-2027 and the car market recovery (+21% Jan-Sep 2026) pull work onshore. Against that, Japanese/Thai captive supply chains, IATF and PPAP approval lead times (often 12-24 months, industry norm, not sourced) and the scale cost gap with China and Thailand hold it back. Much of the gain will go to foreign tier-1s opening in West Java, with Indonesian CNC shops as tier-2/3.

Petrol motorcycles carry 45.2-51.1% TKDN (Astra Honda Motor) and 47.1-58.7% (Yamaha) (TKDN database, 16 Oct 2026). TKDN counts imported raw material as foreign. The share of the billet aftermarket is unknown.
local_makers: PT Astra Honda Motor (Kota Jakarta Utara; Cikampek, Kab. Karawang)
PT Yamaha Indonesia Motor Manufacturing (KIIC, Kab. Karawang; Kota Jakarta Timur)
PT Kawasaki Motor Indonesia (MM2100, Kab. Bekasi)
Tegal metal small firms, tier-2 to AHM (Kab. Tegal)
BRT/PT Bintang Niaga Jaya (city not verified)
cnc_3d_role: CNC is the core: billet aluminium (6061/7075) aftermarket parts such as triple clamps, rearsets, brake and clutch levers, swingarm spools, engine covers, CNC rims, plus OEM tier-2 turned and milled parts (hubs, axles, gears, brackets). 3D printing helps design and fit-check custom accessories before cutting billet, makes small-batch plastic covers, and prints fixtures that hold parts during multi-axis machining.
potential_share: Judgement, 3-5 years: replace 10-20% of the China-origin share of HS 871410 imports, about US$36-72M (estimate: China 57% x US$635.2M = US$359M; x 0.10 and x 0.20). Aftermarket exports could also grow; that is not sized. Reasoning: a large domestic base (6.41M new motorcycles in 2025 per AISI) and an existing export surplus. CNC billet parts sell at about 2x cast prices (Kawahara, snippet), so labour-intensive CNC finishing pays. Against that: Chinese cast/forged parts are cheap, there is no TKDN rule for petrol motorcycles, and OEM parts are captive to the Japanese groups' tier-1s.

product: EV conversion kits and electric-motorcycle components (motors, controller housings, battery enclosures, swingarms); trade figures are a proxy: complete e-motorcycles and e-bikes (HS 871160)
local_now: TKDN database (16 Oct 2026): 102 certified e-motorcycle models from 27 firms, all on Java. Median TKDN 46.4% (range 30.4-75.0%); only 15 models reach the 60% that applies from 1 Jan 2027. No sourced local share for motors, controllers or battery packs. Conversion: 194 conversions by Nov 2023 against a 1,000 target, with 13 licensed workshops (GGGI 2024). About 236,000 e-motorcycles on the road in Oct 2025, under 1% of the fleet (ESDM via Wikipedia).
local_makers: PT Garda Energi Nasional Indonesia/SAVART (Kab. Mojokerto)
PT Yadea Manufaktur Kendaraan Listrik (Kab. Bekasi)
PT Yifang Cargo Mutiara Elektronik/Electrum (Kab. Tangerang)
PT Gesits Motor Nusantara (Cileungsi, Kab. Bogor)
cnc_3d_role: CNC: hub-motor and mid-drive motor housings and end caps (die-cast then machined), shafts, swingarms and pivots, wheel hubs, brake mounts, battery-tray rails and terminals, controller heat-sink housings, conversion-kit motor mounts and adapter plates. 3D printing: fit-check prototypes of enclosures and brackets, low-volume (<1,000/yr) plastic covers and connector housings, sand-printed moulds for first-run aluminium housings, assembly fixtures.
potential_share: Judgement, 3-5 years: if the 60% TKDN rule holds from 2027, locally made shares of machined/cast e-motorcycle metal parts (housings, swingarms, enclosures) in Indonesian-assembled models could reach 60-80%, from an unknown and probably lower base. Most certified models (median 46.4%) need about 14 more TKDN points, and cells and magnets are hard to localise, so metal parts are the cheapest points. The market is small. Estimate: 100,000 units/yr (the government's planned 2026 incentive quota) x Rp1.5-3.0M of machined/cast metal per unit (assumption) = Rp150-300 billion/yr, about US$9-18M at an assumed Rp16,500/US$. Complete e-2W imports (HS 871160) were US$21.2M in 2025, for scale. Conversion kits: 0-5% of this, since the programme stalled (194 conversions by Nov 2023). Reasoning: TKDN pull and planned incentives (Rp5M/unit for 100,000 units, not issued as of Aug 2026) versus weak demand (<1% of 6.41M sales in 2025) and cheap Chinese kits.

local_now: Unknown as a sourced share, but trade shows local assembly dominates: complete bicycles (8712) were exported for US$129.8M and imported for only US$7.8M in 2025 (Comtrade). PT Insera Sena (Polygon, Kab. Sidoarjo) states an annual capacity of one million bicycles. Indonesia is a net exporter of hubs and free-wheels (871493: exports US$37.2M vs imports US$21.7M in 2025) but imports frames (871491: US$74.6M, exports US$3.7M) and rims and spokes (871492: US$39.6M). The TKDN database holds no bicycle certificates.
cnc_3d_role: CNC: hubs, freewheel bodies, cranks and spiders, stems, seat-post heads, dropouts and head tubes for welded aluminium frames, e-bike motor mounts. Welding jigs (CNC-cut). 3D printing: prototype lugs and dropouts, fixtures, and possibly premium printed titanium/aluminium parts (no local evidence).
potential_share: Judgement, 3-5 years: replace 15-30% of frame and fork imports (871491), about US$11-22M (estimate: 0.15 and 0.30 x US$74.6M), anchored on Polygon's Sidoarjo plant and e-bike exports. CNC parts beyond that are small. All bicycle and part imports were US$279.1M in 2025. Reasoning: an existing assembler with exports to the US and EU and a hub export base work for it. Taiwan/China frame costs and no public-procurement pull (no TKDN demand) work against it.

product: Farm machinery and parts (HS 8432, 8433, 8436, 8437; trade figures are the four headings, which include their parts lines 843290, 843390, 843699, 843790)
local_now: TKDN database (16 Oct 2026): 60 firms hold 262 farm-machine certificates, 54 of them on Java. Median certified TKDN: 2-wheel tractors 52.6%, threshers 45.6%, rice milling units 40.8%, 4-wheel tractors 35.9%, transplanters 33.9%, combine harvesters 33.0%. Quick's hand tractors with Kubota RD diesels made in Semarang certify at up to 83.1%; its petrol-engined model is at 40.2%. Quick held up to 70% of the hand-tractor market in 2017 (snippet, pre-2023). Hand-tractor imports (870110) were only US$0.6M in 2025, so hand tractors are almost wholly made locally (Comtrade). Kemenperin: 67 firms, 5,629 workers, US$90M exports in 2024.
local_makers: CV Karya Hidup Sentosa/Quick (Kab. Kulon Progo)
PT Tri Ratna Diesel Indonesia (Kab. Gresik)
cnc_3d_role: CNC: gears, shafts, sprockets and gearbox housings for hand tractors and rotavators; rotary blades, threshing drums and concaves; combine header and track-drive parts; pulleys; machined castings. 3D printing: patterns and core boxes for gearbox and housing castings, scan-to-CAD of worn spares for old Japanese and Chinese machines, prototypes.
potential_share: Judgement, 3-5 years: replace 15-25% of 2025 imports of HS 8432, 8433, 8436 and 8437, about US$63-105M (estimate: 0.15 and 0.25 x US$419.6M). The gain would come by raising combines and 4-wheel tractors from ~33-36% TKDN toward 45-50% with locally machined drivetrain and threshing parts, and by more local hand tractors and threshers. Reasoning: Kementan is a large repeat buyer (7,676 combines in 2020-2026; 16,717 2-wheel and 8,396 4-wheel tractors; 56,000 pumps in 2026), Java makers already hold certificates, and China supplies most imports (cheap but distant support). Against that: Kementan's TKDN floor is only 25%, so imported kits qualify; import costs from China are low; and there is no local engine supply for larger tractors.

cnc_3d_role: CNC and laser/press-brake fabrication of stainless drums, shafts, burr and blade carriers for grinders, roaster drums and bearing housings, huller rolls and RMU parts, cocoa press platens and ball-mill parts, cutter blades. 3D printing: prototypes, guards and chutes, non-food-contact covers; patterns for cast housings.

product: Marine equipment: ship and boat propellers (HS 848710), outboard motors (HS 840721) and their parts, boat fittings (anchors HS 7316 as proxy)
local_now: Unknown as a sourced share. One TKDN-certified propeller maker was found: CV Putra Karya Logam Sukses (Kab. Asahan), brass propellers at 72.7-83.4% TKDN. No TKDN certificate exists for outboard motors (0 results for 'motor tempel', 'mesin tempel', 'outboard', 16 Oct 2026). About 70% of shipyard components were imported in 2015 (pre-2023). 2025 imports: propellers US$27.7M, outboard motors US$30.2M (Comtrade).
local_makers: CV Putra Karya Logam Sukses (Simpang Empat, Kab. Asahan, North Sumatra)
Tegal metal small firms with BKI-certified ship components (Kab. Tegal; 2015)
PT Karya Marina Mandiri, fishing boats (Kota Jakarta Utara)
cnc_3d_role: CNC: propeller hub boring and keyways, blade finishing and pitch correction, dynamic balancing; propeller shafts, stern tubes, couplings, rudder stocks; stainless and bronze fittings (cleats, fairleads, bollards); outboard spare parts (skegs, brackets, propellers). 3D printing: printed blade and hub patterns or sand moulds for each diameter/pitch (replacing hand-carved wooden patterns), pitch-checking templates, and prototypes of fittings.
potential_share: Judgement, 3-5 years: small-boat propellers could take 30-50% of propeller imports, about US$8-14M (estimate: 0.30 and 0.50 x US$27.7M), plus shafts and stern gear for KKP's planned 1,000 x 30 GT boats. Large classed ship propellers stay imported. Outboard motors: 0-5% (US$0-1.5M), parts only, since no local engine maker exists. Marine diesel engines (840810, not in this line's total) were a larger and rising import (US$205.6M in 2025). Reasoning: high certified TKDN is possible (Asahan 73-83%), casting skills exist in Tegal, Juwana and Ceper, and KKP's 1,582-vessel plan works for it. Against that: the vessel plan is not yet a pipeline, BKI class approval is needed for classed vessels, and Japanese/Chinese outboard brands hold the market.

local_now: TKDN database (16 Oct 2026): 55 firms hold 265 irrigation/farm-pump certificates (median TKDN 40.0%, range 25.7-84.3%; a lower bound), and 73 of 74 pump firms are on Java. Kementan bought 734 TKDN-certified pumps in its 2022 pre-harvest round (pre-2023). The market share of local pumps is unknown.

cnc_3d_role: Casting plus CNC: volute casings, impellers (turning, balancing), pump shafts and sleeves, mechanical-seal seats, engine flanges and couplings, base frames; small-engine parts (crankshafts, cam gears) for local engine assemblers. 3D printing: patterns and core boxes for casings and impellers across 2-6 inch sizes, prototype impellers for flow tests.
